reason: The fibroblast conditions specify a differentiation route for a subset of the stem-cell population, which should lead toward supporting material.
expectation: A subset of the stem cells will develop into fibroblasts.

effect: The fibroblast lineage now has collagen RNA messages, linking differentiation to production of supporting material.
reaction: The unchanged DNA and newly active collagen genes make the distinction between lineage and gene expression clear.
reason: Collagen is a protein, so the cells should use the available amino acids to make it from their messages.
expectation: The fibroblast-lineage cells will synthesize collagen or a collagen precursor.

effect: The fibroblasts have made collagen precursors and packaged them for secretion, so extracellular fluid is the next plausible step.
reaction: The ER and Golgi processing makes the route from RNA to secreted material clearer.
reason: The precursors are in secretory vesicles, and the extracellular fluid includes processing enzymes outside the cells.
expectation: The fibroblasts will release collagen precursors that form supporting material outside the cells.

effect: The collagen precursors were secreted and assembled into extracellular matrix, completing the supporting-material goal. The muscle branch remains.
reaction: The distinction between living cells and the supporting material they secrete is clear.
reason: The skeletal-muscle conditions describe a route from unspecialized cells to muscle precursors.
expectation: A separate subset of stem-cell descendants will develop into muscle-forming precursors.

effect: A separate muscle lineage now has RNA messages for muscle proteins, but the cells are not yet mature fibres.
reaction: The parallel with collagen production makes the different gene-expression paths clear.
reason: The muscle messages and shared amino acid supply suggest the cells can now make muscle proteins.
expectation: The muscle-lineage cells will synthesize proteins needed for muscle formation.

effect: The muscle lineage used its RNA messages and amino acids to make muscle proteins, completing the goal while remaining separate precursor cells rather than mature fibres.
reaction: The explicit distinction between myoblasts and fused muscle fibres was useful.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making and secreting collagen was most worthwhile: the planned illustrations connect gene expression and protein processing to material that supports cells outside the membrane.

leastWorthwhile.text: The muscle branch repeated the differentiation-then-amino-acids pattern, making its choices fairly predictable, though the parallel reinforced the lesson.

surprise.text: The collagen precursors were processed and assembled outside the cells into fibrils and fibres, rather than simply appearing as finished matrix inside them.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless. The differentiation conditions were broad inputs rather than named signals, but their planned descriptions made their role and timing clear.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the two lineages show how the same inherited DNA can support different work, and the unfinished development of muscle precursors leaves a meaningful next question.
